nodes.summary: Applying the denotation of $\lambda.M$ to $v$ gives the denotation of $M$ with the new bound variable valued by $v$: This is Scott's graph theorem $\operatorname{app}(\operatorname{graph}(f), \cdot) = f$, applied to the continuous function that the body denotes.
nodes.title: β at the level of denotations

nodes.summary: In the graph model, the paradoxical combinator $Y$ applied to any $u \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ denotes the least fixed point $\bigcup_k \operatorname{app}(u, \cdot)^k(\emptyset)$ of the continuous function determined by $u$ (D. Scott, *Data types as lattices*, SIAM J. Comput. 5(3) (1976), 522–587, Theorem 2.5). So recursion is λ-definable in $P(\omega)$, and the least fixed points given by the fixed-point theorem are…
nodes.title: Scott's first recursion theorem

nodes.summary: For a value $v \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and a valuation $bs : \mathbb{N} \to P(\omega)$ of de Bruijn indices, $v \cdot bs$ sends index $0$ to $v$ and index $n + 1$ to $bs(n)$. It is the valuation under one more binder, with the new bound variable valued by $v$.
nodes.title: Extending a bound-variable environment

nodes.summary: If every bound index occurring in $M$ (counted from the outside) is below $k$, then $[\![M]\!]_{\rho, bs}$ depends only on $bs(0), \ldots, bs(k-1)$. Here "below $k$" is CSLib's `LcAt k`.
nodes.title: Denotations depend only on the bound variables in scope

nodes.summary: A locally closed term (CSLib's `LC`: no dangling de Bruijn index) has the same denotation under every valuation of bound variables.
nodes.title: Locally closed terms ignore the bound-variable environment

nodes.summary: If $(\lambda.M)\,N$ contracts to $M[N]$ (CSLib's β-step, with $\lambda.M$ and $N$ locally closed), both sides have the same denotation in $P(\omega)$ under all valuations (D. Scott, *Data types as lattices*, SIAM J. Comput. 5(3) (1976), 522–587, Theorem 2.2, the rule β).
nodes.title: Soundness of a β-contraction in the graph model

nodes.summary: One step of full β-reduction, contracting a redex anywhere in a term, including under λ, preserves the denotation in $P(\omega)$ under every valuation of free and bound variables. This is the β rule of Scott's conversion theorem together with the instance of the rule ξ that full β-reduction needs (D. Scott, *Data types as lattices*, SIAM J. Comput. 5(3) (1976), 522–587, Theorem 2.2). Scott's ξ is the equivalence…
nodes.title: Soundness of full β-reduction in the graph model

nodes.summary: If $M$ reduces to $N$ in any number of full β-steps, then $M$ and $N$ have the same denotation in $P(\omega)$, under every valuation. In particular β-convertible closed terms have equal denotations.
nodes.title: Soundness of multi-step full β-reduction in the graph model

nodes.summary: The closed normal forms $K = \lambda x.\lambda y.x$ and $K^* = \lambda x.\lambda y.y$ have different denotations in $P(\omega)$: applied to $\emptyset$ and then to $\mathbb{N}$, they give $\emptyset$ and $\mathbb{N}$. So the model does not identify all terms. This rules out the degenerate one-point model, in which every equation holds.
nodes.title: The graph model separates `λx.λy.x` from `λx.λy.y`

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a term whose denotation does not depend on the bound-variable valuation, for instance a locally closed term. Opening the bound variable $i$ of $M$ with $s$ (CSLib's $M⟦i ↝ s⟧$) denotes $M$ with index $i$ valued by the denotation of $s$: This is the semantic counterpart of substitution, and the key lemma for the soundness of β.
nodes.title: Substitution lemma for opening

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ value the free variables and $bs$ the bound variables (de Bruijn indices) of CSLib's locally nameless untyped λ-terms in $P(\omega)$. The denotation $[\![M]\!]_{\rho, bs} \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is defined by recursion on $M$:
nodes.title: Denotation of an untyped λ-term in the graph model

nodes.summary: For a free variable $x$, the η-redex $\lambda y.\, x\,y$ and $x$ have different denotations under a suitable valuation of $x$. The reason is that $\operatorname{graph}(\operatorname{app}(u, \cdot)) \ne u$ for some $u$. Scott's conversion theorem lists only the rules α, β and ξ as valid in $P(\omega)$ (D. Scott, *Data types as lattices*, SIAM J. Comput. 5(3) (1976), 522–587, Theorem 2.2 and the remarks after its…
nodes.title: The η-rule is not sound in the graph model

nodes.summary: For every term $M$ and valuation $bs$ of its bound variables, the denotation $\rho \mapsto [\![M]\!]_{\rho, bs}$ is a Scott-continuous function of the valuation $\rho$ of the free variables, ordered pointwise. This is the form of Scott's continuity theorem in which the variables of a term are its free variables (D. Scott, *Data types as lattices*, SIAM J. Comput. 5(3) (1976), 522–587, Theorem 2.1: LAMBDA-definable…
nodes.title: Denotations are Scott-continuous in the free variables

nodes.summary: For every term $M$ and valuation $\rho$ of its free variables, the denotation $bs \mapsto [\![M]\!]_{\rho, bs}$ is a Scott-continuous function of the values of the bound variables (D. Scott, *Data types as lattices*, SIAM J. Comput. 5(3) (1976), 522–587, Theorem 2.1, there for all terms of the language LAMBDA). The proof is by induction on $M$. For abstraction it uses that $\operatorname{graph}$ commutes with…
nodes.title: Scott's continuity theorem for the graph model

nodes.summary: The closed term $Y = \lambda u.(\lambda x.\,u(x\,x))(\lambda x.\,u(x\,x))$, written with de Bruijn indices as $\lambda.(\lambda.1\,(0\,0))\,(\lambda.1\,(0\,0))$ (D. Scott, *Data types as lattices*, SIAM J. Comput. 5(3) (1976), 522–587, equation (2.8)).
nodes.title: The paradoxical combinator `Y`

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
